summary: Publish categorical agent observations as replaceable current registers while retaining durable numeric accounting and diagnostics. Native prompt alerts read current registers; terminal refusals record an opaque prompt reference instead of using an ephemeral register ID as durable claim evidence. Modern driver ownership and transition counters keep a cleared prompt stable across heartbeat restamps; a new transition or register epoch opens a new episode.

replay.detail: Durable graph replay is unchanged. Current registers are outside graph replay and are refreshed by their live owners.

schema.detail: Adds latest_values, latest_readiness and local indexes plus current-value epoch and feed-boundary metadata. No numeric staging migration or graph backfill is introduced. Older binaries can open the additive schema. Adds a partial index over retained pending numeric usage for bounded background recovery. Adds a local quarantined_events spool table lazily when an invalid or positively retired event is retained; spool version stays unchanged. Current record envelopes add _semantic_transition metadata; receivers conservatively invalidate when older senders omit it. Adds semantic frontier clocks and resumable legacy-history retirement cursors. Older register databases initialize clocks in transactions of at most 64 keys without parsing claim history. Collector tombstones consume the same SQLite AUTOINCREMENT clock as register and timeline rows; reopen reconciles a prior frontier that exceeded that clock. Adds an indexed kind/subject/slot cursor for refusal-directed collection.

rules.detail: No claim kind, checkpoint rule or durable numeric accounting retention rule changes.

compatibility.detail: Categorical status, context occupancy, todo, workspace and connectivity use one-shot current publication. Register-backed status-history returns empty items with complete=false and retained_from=now. Current values use request-time state even at a pinned graph cut; a missed heartbeat can produce staleness after 90 seconds. Old peers without current-value transport appear frozen then stale until upgraded. Numeric usage, limits, accounting stops, diagnostics and timeline keep durable publication and retries. Accounting stops use an additive accounting_stop marker on the existing harness-context spool kind; older drivers decode its ordinary context record, ignore that marker and consume the event. The new local native-only /v1/harness-events/usage-flush route returns a terminal compatibility miss on older daemons rather than blocking the spool. Unconfirmed launch fences retain numeric events for retry. Invalid and positively retired numeric events move atomically into local quarantine with their original incarnation, payload and reason; they never change the successor runtime. Nonzero-sequence legacy events retain their reliable replay protocol. Fresh live-provider observation heartbeats run every 30 seconds independently of five-minute presence refreshes. OpenCode gives each provider its own initial heartbeat phase within that interval so simultaneous launches do not keep colliding at the current-value writer. A native mailbox launch can await its running observation without an accepted starting-status sample, using the same authenticated live launch proof after normal admission refuses graph readiness. A starting bind has a 60-second deadline including retries and requests; provider, retired-token and terminal fences remain final. A register write that reaches its own 100 ms SQLite deadline returns HTTP 503 with code current-value-deadline. Updated drivers drop that sample once without retaining a retry and also accept the legacy internal interrupted response from older daemons. Older drivers can propagate a typed 503 from their starting handshake and terminate that launch; this one-shot guarantee requires the updated driver. Unchanged heartbeat restamps refresh source time and identity without bumping aggregate or per-kind collection revisions, advancing roster frontiers, or waking sockets; state, reason, ownership and stale-to-fresh recovery still invalidate the affected windows. Cached agent pages refresh same-incarnation observation timestamps through indexed register lookups without folding the roster again. Received seat registers require a declared agent on the publishing host even without running evidence, and each observation kind has a separate 10,000-key capacity; existing keys remain replaceable. Bounded background passes collect undeclared or retired seats and observations of hosts outside the current fleet, and capacity refusals are logged. Authenticated fleet members are mutually trusted observers, while durable runtime evidence retains the incarnation fence. A failed fleet membership refresh skips collection and is not cached as an empty fleet. Capacity refusals wake the collector and temporarily increase its sweep cadence. Current write admission uses the remaining unchanged 100 ms attempt, reserving 10 ms for the register write (at most 90 ms admission); busy BEGIN retries use at most 1 ms intervals inside that same attempt, with validation and mutation only after admission. It adds no later retry obligation or graph-writer job. An agents window overtaken by newer roster publications releases its physical read and rechecks once at a fresh snapshot without folding cards; an overtaken HTTP first page also rechecks its cut once. Continuations still require their original published cut. Capacity exhaustion returns HTTP 503 current-value-capacity for a new peer key while existing keys remain replaceable. Refusal-driven collection scans that kind first, with a 100 ms minimum pass interval even under notification pressure. Current register attempts reserve an empty managed-writer turn within the unchanged 100 ms bound; expired reservations publish nothing, and no sample or retry obligation is queued. Incremental replication keeps one previous immutable Agents publication per current/history mode, with its own cut and time, until a coherent replacement or full reset. Fallback reads do not advance roster revisions and cannot satisfy fresh=true, including at an admitted but unprojected target. Updated Pi-family channels retry the legacy HTTP 500 internal task-number cancellation reply only during post-hello todo activation when daemon shutdown cancels the startup reader; older in-memory channels can terminate during that activation on this reply. Current writers reuse one exclusively checked-out connection per store instead of parsing the schema for every sample. Checkout, schema checks, managed admission and mutation share the same 100 ms attempt; errors, epoch changes and full resets discard the connection, schema changes clear its prepared statements before use, and a schema change during a successful loan discards the returned connection. A loan returned with an open transaction is rolled back and discarded. No observation is queued for a later attempt.

downtime.detail: No daemon downtime or seat interruption is required for ordinary upgrades. Fleet operations preserves existing seats and installs the CI release artifact.

manual.detail: Upgrade all peers to receive current values. Signed-log restore creates a new current-value epoch. A filesystem-copy restore preserves its old epoch and may rewind counters: before starting the restored daemon, remove only current-value-epoch from the offline database meta table so open initializes a later epoch; ensure the host clock has moved forward. Restart native producers with fresh runtime incarnations. Restarting producers alone does not recover rewound workspace or transport counters. Install the updated st release artifact to obtain the independent stop-flush guarantee; during mixed versions the old accounting publication behavior remains, and skipped stop markers or missing routes are logged. Existing seats remain running during the operator-managed upgrade. The daemon and drivers ship in the same st executable. Install the updated executable before restarting the daemon and use it for new launches; an existing driver process keeps its older in-memory code until re-exec. Such a process can propagate typed starting-handshake 503 errors under the new daemon. The live-launch bootstrap retry is bounded at 60 seconds and can distinguish a successor from predecessor runtime evidence; old drivers lack that recovery path.

recovery.detail: Dropped current samples are never replayed; a new owner sample refreshes the register. Ordinary reopen preserves the database epoch. Feed cursor gaps require snapshot resynchronization. Durable accounting and control obligations remain in their outboxes across daemon outages and driver re-exec. Failed retained-usage subjects do not block later subjects; a bounded per-subject backoff retains their pending slots. Provider completion spends at most 45 seconds draining retained accounting and requesting the stop flush, leaving unpublished events spooled on expiry. Unknown publication failures and future schemas remain retryable. Same-incarnation failed runtime evidence is terminal. Quarantined records remain local for inspection and are not automatically replayed. Quarantine retains at most 256 records and 64 MiB of payloads, pruning oldest inspection evidence first. A retained event with 100 publication refusals attempts an idempotent visible accounting-publication-stalled diagnostic at most once per minute; its bounded counter survives re-exec without acknowledging the event. Rolling back the daemon makes it ignore current registers. The first modern sample retires legacy categorical slots and schedules their local observation history for bounded background retirement (at most 256 rows per transaction), preserving numeric usage rows, so those deleted rows are not restored by a binary rollback; categorical status stays frozen or stale until older publishers refresh it. Durable numeric series, diagnostics and accounting remain retained. Collected register payloads release capacity; one small semantic clock per observed subject remains as a tombstone so deletions cannot rewind reader frontiers. Legacy history payload inspection runs read-only before its own bounded transaction, separately from register collection, so a failing history job cannot roll back reclaimed register capacity. New keys without older local history do not enqueue retirement work. A malformed usage-history retirement job is skipped after its exact cursor/cutoff is rechecked; only the scheduling row is removed, its original payloads are retained under ordinary local-observation retention, and later jobs continue. The skip is logged after commit.
